title: ServiceTokenClaims
description: Claims of a short-lived RS256 client-credentials token issued by OpenVibe.Network to a service, app, mod, node or agent principal. Replaces X-Internal-Key. App tokens (actor_type app) also carry project_id and env; receivers refuse env=sandbox unless they opted in. Agent tokens (actor_type agent; roadmap WS-Z2, docs/t2-projects-and-grants.md) are minted for an agent by its host and also carry project_id, env and on_behalf_of (the owner), and act (the host).

iss.description: Issuer; https://openvibe.network in production. Receivers pass the issuer they expect to verifyServiceToken().

cap.description: Granted capability ids; a trailing .* grants a family. For an agent: only the delegated grants whose effective mode is auto.

ns.description: Namespace constraints, e.g. live.* or mod.example.*. A developer app token carries its project_id (the whole project, as issued before namespaces were rows) and app.<project_id>.*: on Media, app.<project_id> and app.<project_id>.sandbox are the project's production and sandbox namespaces, with children below them.

project_id.description: Developer project of an app principal (ADR-014). Services key tenancy by it. Absent on first-party service tokens.

env.description: Environment of an app principal. A receiver MUST refuse env=sandbox (401 token.sandbox_refused) unless it opted in to sandbox tokens. Absent on first-party service tokens, which are production.

on_behalf_of.description: The person an app or agent acts for: on an app token, the person who authorized it through the authorization-code flow (absent on client_credentials tokens); on an agent token, the agent's owner (always present).

cap_confirm.description: Agent tokens only: delegated capabilities whose every use needs an approved confirmation request (network.confirmation-request@1) or a standing rule. Exact ids, never a family. Disjoint from cap. A receiver answers 403 confirmation.required without a usable OpenVibe-Confirmation header.

sub.description: The host that minted the token for the agent: a developer app of the agent's project and environment, or a first-party service.

act.description: Agent tokens only (RFC 8693 actor claim): the host acting for the agent.
